# Estimates of temporary employment

In this exercise, you can recreate ONS labour market analysis reported in the table [EMP07 Temporary Employees](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/datasets/temporaryemployeesemp07). Currently, this table is updated four times a year in February, May, August and November using the Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS).

Learning outcomes:

-   To become more familiar with QLFS datasets.
-   To become more familiar with the weighting variable.

## Data

The data used relates to an estimate for Oct-December 2020.

To follow the exercise, you need to access the relevant dataset from the UK Data Service: [Quarterly Labour Force Survey, October - December, 2020](http://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-SN-8777-3).

## Get set-up

One you have downloaded the data, save it some where accessible.

```{r}
library(haven)
library(tidyverse)
library (sjmisc) #used for some of the tables 
```

```{r}
#setwd ("~/LFS_exercises")

#Open data and keep relevant variables.
lfs_od20 <- haven::read_sav("data/UKDA-8777-spss/spss/spss28/lfsp_od20_eul_pwt24.sav")

```

Inspect the dataset including the number of cases and variables.

```{r}
dim(lfs_od20) 

```

As the dataset is large, let's save a copy with just the variables we will use.

```{r}
data <- lfs_od20 %>% 
  select(PERSNO, PWT24, JBTP101, FTPT, INECAC05, JOBTYP, SEX)

head(data)
```

### Examine variables

Now let's examine key variables in the dataset.

```{r}
data %>% select(JBTP101, FTPT, INECAC05, JOBTYP, SEX) %>% frq()

```

```{r}
misscheck <- haven::read_sav("data/UKDA-8777-spss/spss/spss28/lfsp_od20_eul_pwt24.sav", user_na = TRUE)

table(misscheck$JOBTYP)

```

### Apply the weight (simple)

Apply the weight and examine the variable frequencies again.

```{r}

# Define the variables you want to analyze
variables <- c("JBTP101", "FTPT", "INECAC05", "JOBTYP", "SEX")

# Apply frq() to each variable with weights
lapply(variables, function(var) frq(data[[var]], weights = data$PWT24))

```

Create a variable to indicate those working part time.

```{r}
mydata1$PartTime <- rec(mydata1$FTPT,rec="2,4=1; else=0")

mydata1$PartTime <-sjlabelled::set_labels(mydata1$PartTime, labels = c("Part Time"))
```

### REVIEW QUESTIONS

When making the table below, which cases are selected in the filter?

head(mydata1$JOBTYP)
head(mydata1$INECAC05)

#split by sex and part-time

mydata1 %\>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1 & SEX==1) %\>% uncount(weights = .\$PWT20) %\>%\

mydata1 %\>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1 & SEX==2) %\>% uncount(weights = .\$PWT20) %\>%\
tab(PartTime, JobTmp)

Finally, get unweighted frequencies.

```{r}
mydata1 %>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1) %>%tab(JobTmp, PartTime)
```
